AddAssets.description:
Add imported assets with the provenance their import filled in
(11.39). The only way a non-font asset enters a scene.

AddFonts.description:
Add prepared fonts and the font assets their faces need (11.13).
The only way a font enters a scene.

ApplyPreset.description: Instantiate one phase of a starter motion preset at `atFrame`.

AssetApproval.description: A named person's approval of an asset for use.

at.description:
When they approved, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp. Authoring metadata
only: nothing on the render path reads it (invariant 8).

user.description: The approving user, as the authorization layer names them (2.9).

AssetAvailability.description: Whether an asset's bytes are available where they are needed.

AssetKind.description:
The kind of thing an asset is. `Font` is here so the asset store and the
font subsystem agree on what a font asset is.

AssetLibraryItem.description:
An asset as the library knows it. Carries **both** addresses: the content
hash (immutable, addresses the store) and the project-relative path
(mutable, addresses the library). The hash is what a scene's bindings
resolve against, so re-importing over the same path — a new render of the
same logo — updates the hash but never the binding.

assetId.description: Stable scene-facing id. Survives relink; distinct from any storage id.

checksum.description: Content hash — the store address. `None` only while importing.

name.description: Display name, separate from the on-disk name (ADR-0002 B.3).

provenance.description:
Where the bytes came from and under what terms (11.39). Every record
carries one, and it is always written: a human-made asset may leave
every field empty, but the schema is present in every saved project.

AssetOrigin.description: Who or what produced an asset's content.

oneOf.description: A person made it, including a file a person brought into the project.

A deterministic tool derived it from other inputs: a conversion, an
export or a render.
A generative model produced it.

AssetProvenance.description: Where an asset's bytes came from and under what terms.

c2paManifest.description: An attached C2PA manifest: a project-relative path or a URI.

promptHash.description:
SHA-256 of the prompt a model was given. The prompt text is not
stored with the asset.

provider.description:
Who supplied the bytes: a font service, a stock library, a model
vendor.

sources.description:
What the asset was made or fetched from: file names, URLs, the content
hashes of input assets. Always written, so the field is visible in a
saved project even when it is empty.

CloseScene.description: Close a session; a dirty session refuses unless `force`.

ColorValue.description:
An authored paint: nothing, a colour, or a gradient.

`None` is a value, not an absence — "the author turned the fill off" and
"the author has not set a fill" are different states, and collapsing them
is how a transparent object becomes a black one on the other renderer.
Ported from 1.x `ColorValue`, with every colour now tagged.

angle.description: Degrees, clockwise from the positive X axis.

ConfirmDesignSystem.description: Confirm a design-system draft as the project's next version.

ContentHash.description: Content address of asset bytes: SHA-256, lowercase hex.

ControlField.description: One named property an operator is allowed to fill on a template.

ControlFieldKind.description: The kind of value an operator may enter for a declared field.

ControlValue.description: A typed value supplied to a declared control field.

CreateProject.description: Create an empty project in the store.

CubicBezier.description:
Cubic-bezier control points for a custom outgoing easing.

`x1` and `x2` stay in 0–1 because they are time controls; y may overshoot
provided the resulting segment stays within the property's range (opacity
0–1, width/height non-negative). Other properties permit overshoot.
The points are stored with the
key, not solved from neighbouring keys at display time, so a saved scene
means the same curve when it is reopened.

DesignSystemCommit.description:
A draft plus the human confirming it (G.2, build plan 10.4).

The confirmation is deliberately *not* a field on [`DesignSystemDraft`]. A
draft is a proposal, and a proposal that can carry its own confirmation is
one an importer could fill in on the reviewer's behalf — which is exactly
the auto-accept G.2 forbids. Keeping it in the request makes confirming an
act a caller performs rather than a property the draft already had.

confirmedBy.description: Who accepted it. Recorded into provenance; never invented.

DesignSystemDraft.description: A lossless import proposal. It cannot become active without confirmation.

DesignSystemSource.description:
The complete source document retained beside an imported draft.

Import is deliberately not a destructive projection. The mapped tokens are
what GrapiX can enforce; `document` is the source **as supplied**, so a
reviewer can inspect and re-export everything it actually contained.

It is the original text rather than a re-print of the parse, and `sha256`
is taken over those same bytes. A hash over a re-serialisation answers "is
this equivalent to what we parsed?", which is not the question provenance
asks: a duplicated JSON key, or a number re-spelled by whichever toolchain
last wrote the file, would silently change what the record refers to.

DesignSystemSourceKind.description: The external format a design-system draft came from.

DraftVisualTokens.description:
Visual tokens while an import is awaiting human review.

`min_text_size` stays optional here and required in [`VisualTokens`]. An
importer may not invent a legibility threshold merely to make a draft look
complete; confirmation refuses until a human supplies one.

DuplicateScene.description: Copy a stored scene under a new id and name.

EditProperty.description: A property value edit; with `autoKey` it also upserts a key at `frame`.

EditScene.description:
Apply an ordered, atomic edit batch to one document. One batch is
one undo entry, tagged with the module that issued it.

EditorModule.description:
The Editor module a gesture came from (11.37). Undo scoped to a module
reverses only batches tagged with it; an untagged batch belongs to
`Scene`. The surface that issues a gesture names its own module, because
guessing it from edit kinds would misfile a gesture that touches several.

EmbeddingPolicy.description:
Whether a font's bytes may travel inside a `.gpxpkg` — the licensing
decision made per font (docs/p2-licensing-positions.md §5).

oneOf.description: Bytes may be packaged (licence permits redistribution: OFL, Apache…).
Package carries the reference; the render node resolves and caches.
Workstation-only; bytes never leave the operator's machine.

FontDefinition.description:
A family as the scene knows it: its faces, fallbacks and licensing
posture. Embedded verbatim in the scene document, so a package is
self-describing.

license.description:
The declared licence. A `Package` font without one is a preflight
refusal (p2-licensing-positions §5: unstated licence ⇒ restricted).

FontFaceDefinition.description: One face of a family: weight/style/stretch with a source.

FontFormat.description:
Font container formats the pipeline accepts. WOFF/WOFF2 are delivery
wrappers; the shaper sees the same tables either way.

FontLoadStatus.description:
Load state of a font or face. `Missing` at preflight is a refusal
(`Refusal::FontMissing`), never a fallback to a system font.

oneOf.description: Linked source declared but not yet resolved; cannot preflight.

FontSource.description:
Where a face's bytes come from.

`rename_all_fields` (not `rename_all`) because the variant *fields* are
what hit the wire: `rename_all` alone would leave `asset_id` snake_case
while every other contract is camelCase.

oneOf.description: Packaged asset bytes, content-addressed.

originalUrl.description: Original public URL when this face was resolved and cached from CSS.

stylesheetUrl.description: Stylesheet that declared this cached face.

oneOf.description: A CSS stylesheet declaring `@font-face` rules (Google Fonts class).
An Adobe Fonts project. Reference-only by licence; never packaged.
A direct HTTPS font file URL.

GradientCoordinateMode.description:
Whether a gradient's coordinates are the object's or the scene's. An
object-space gradient follows its object; a scene-space one stays put
while the object moves through it.

GradientSpread.description: What a gradient does outside its 0–1 span. CSS's own names.

KeyRef.description: One authored key a capture names: a property and the frame it sits on.

LicenseClass.description:
The terms an asset may be used under, as a class a show profile can test
(13.8) rather than free licence text.

oneOf.description: Made by or for the production, which holds the rights.
Third-party, licensed for commercial broadcast.

An open licence that permits commercial use: OFL, CC0, CC BY,
Apache-2.0, MIT.
GPL-class: obligations attach when it is redistributed.
Licensed for non-commercial use only, such as CC BY-NC.
Licensed for editorial or news use only.
Limited by territory, term or medium.

MotionTokens.description:
Motion tokens: the primitives every preset composes from (G.6.1).

Durations and staggers are milliseconds. Easings are cubic-bezier control
points, or the literal `hold` for a phase that must not interpolate.

stagger.description: Named stagger intervals in ms, e.g. `tight: 40`, `base: 70`.

NamedEasing.description: An easing token: a cubic-bezier curve, or `hold`.

oneOf.description: A named cubic-bezier: `[x1, y1, x2, y2]`.
A named hold: no interpolation between keys.

ObjectField.description:
A typed inspector field/value pair. The adjacent tag makes an invalid field
and value combination unrepresentable on the command wire.

OpenScene.description: Open a document in a new session.

PhaseKind.description:
The operator phases a scene timeline can name.

These are exactly `crate::mcp::MOTION_PHASES`, and a test below pins them
against it: a phase added to one and not the other fails the gate rather
than producing a scene the agent surface cannot describe.

oneOf.description: Build on. Triggered by Take.
Idle loop after `in` completes. Interruptible at any frame.
Build off. Triggered by Out.
A staged build, triggered by Continue. A timeline may carry several.
How a bound value changes on air without a full re-take.

ProvenanceTool.description: The tool, or for model origin the model, that made or imported the bytes.

Redo.description: Reapply the latest undone batch, or the latest one `module` issued.

RelinkAsset.description: Point a library asset at new bytes, keeping its id and bindings.

RelinkMaterial.description: Repoint every use of one material to another.

RemoveFont.description:
Remove one font nothing names, with the font assets no other font
uses. The only way a font leaves a scene.

ReplaceControl.description: Replace the declared control with the same `fieldId`.

Rgba.description:
A colour, with the space it was authored in.

Components are 0–1 floats rather than 8-bit bytes because the working
space is linear and 8 bits of linear has visible banding in the shadows.

SaveMotionPreset.description:
Save the selected keys of one object as one phase of a motion
preset in the project's library (11.15). The document is read, never
written: saving a preset is not a scene edit and is not undoable.

oneOf.description: Update the stored scene the session is bound to; it must exist.
Create the scene in a project; it must not exist. Binds the session.
Write a scene file.

SceneEasing.description:
The easing between two keys. Closed and finite: the curve an author chooses
must be one every evaluator knows by name, because a substituted curve is a
visual change no one named (invariant 18).

SceneEdit.description:
One change to one scene document. Only carried inside
`EditorCommand::EditScene` and only applied through [`apply_edits`].

SceneKeyframe.description: One key on one numeric property channel.

bezier.description: Custom bezier control points, present exactly when easing is custom.

easing.description: Outgoing easing toward the next key.

frame.description: Absolute frame at the scene canvas rate.

value.description: The property's value at that frame, in the property's own units.

oneOf.description: A fresh document built in Rust by `scene::new_scene`.
A scene file on disk.
A stored project scene; an already-open origin is reused.

SceneTarget.description:
The document an edit batch applies to: an open session, or a scene in the
project store (read, edited and written back in one command).

SessionKey.description:
Identity of one open editor session. A `u32`, so TS receives `number`
rather than `bigint` (memory rule 22). Keys are monotonic from 1.

SetBinding.description: Bind `property` to a data path, or unbind it when `path` is absent.

SetObjectField.description: One inspector field over every listed object.

SetSceneId.description: Change the id of a scene that is not bound to a stored origin.

SourceColorSpace.description:
What a colour or a texture was authored in. There is no `Unknown`: an
untagged source is a defect the importer must refuse, not a value a
renderer may guess at (B.1, "never infer").

oneOf.description:
IEC 61966-2-1. What a hex literal, a PNG without an ICC profile and
most authoring tools mean.
Already linear — no decode on the way in.
ITU-R BT.709 with its own transfer curve. Broadcast source material.

StyleColor.description:
A text-style colour, either literal or resolved from the active project
design system when the style is applied.

StyleNumber.description:
A numeric text-style value, either literal or resolved from the active
project design system when the style is applied.

TakePage.description: A saved operator-filled instance of a template.

TextCase.description:
Case applied when the text is drawn, not when it is typed: the authored
characters stay as they are, so a data binding can replace the text and
the case still applies, and switching it off returns the author's own
capitalisation.

TextStyle.description:
A named, reusable subset of a text object's appearance.

Optional entries are deliberately absent rather than defaults: applying a
style must not overwrite a property its author did not declare.

TimelinePhase.description: One named span of the scene timeline.

endFrame.description: One past the last frame. See the module note on why this is exclusive.

name.description:
Distinguishes several `continue` phases from each other. Absent means
the kind names it uniquely, which is true of every kind but `continue`.

startFrame.description: First frame of the phase, inclusive.

TokenMapping.description: One source value that became a GrapiX token.

TokenRef.description:
A token reference in a preset: `{duration.base}`, `{easing.brand-in}`.

A preset that hardcodes a value instead of referencing a token is a bug for
the same reason a component hardcoding a hex colour is (G.6.1). Kept as a
string with a checked shape rather than a free string, so a malformed
reference is caught at parse, not at render.

Undo.description: Reverse the latest applied batch, or the latest one `module` issued.

UnexpressibleToken.description:
A source value the current token contract cannot express.

Keeping the original value is part of the report: a path and a vague
message are not enough for a human to judge whether accepting the draft
would discard a load-bearing brand rule.

UpdateKeyframe.description: Replace a key that already exists at `keyframe.frame`.
